'''''Diospyros nigra''''', the '''black sapote''', is a species of [[persimmon]]. Common names include '''chocolate pudding fruit''', '''black soapapple''' and (in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]) '''''zapote prieto'''''.  The tropical fruit tree is native to Mexico, Central America, and Colombia.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> The common name sapote refers to any soft, edible fruit. Black sapote is not related to [[white sapote]] and is only distantly related to [[mamey sapote]]. The genus ''Diospyros'' has numerous other fruit bearing tree species in addition to the persimmons and black sapote. It is said to taste like chocolate pudding.<ref>{{Cite news |title=The winter fruit that tastes like chocolate pudding |url=https://www.delicious.com.au/people-events/produce-awards/article/guide-black-sapote-aka-chocolate-pudding-fruit/izk3yk56|last=Welsh|first=Caitlin|date=8 August 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The etymology of Diospyros is "divine fruit". It derives from the greek words "dios" and "pyron". This term, translated from [[Greek Language|Greek]], can be variously rendered as  "God's pear", "Wheat of Zeus" and "Jove's fire".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Persimmon |url=https://creative.colorado.edu/~hayu7527/web/persimmonwiki.html |access-date=2022-12-13 |archive-date=2022-10-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221013000411/https://creative.colorado.edu/~hayu7527/web/persimmonwiki.html }}</ref>

==Description==
Mature trees can grow to over {{convert|25|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height and are [[evergreen]]. It is frost sensitive but can tolerate light frosts. The [[leaf|leaves]] are elliptic-oblong, tapered at both ends, dark green, glossy and {{convert|10|-|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. Some trees bear only male flowers. Others have both male and female flowers, though some of these are self-incompatible.<ref name=Morton>{{cite web|last=Morton|first=Julia|author-link=Julia Morton|title=Black Sapote|url=http://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/morton/black_sapote.html|work=Fruits of warm climates|access-date=6 March 2013|page=416|year=1987}}</ref><ref name="w-a-f">[http://www.worldagroforestrycentre.org/sea/Products/AFDbases/af/asp/SpeciesInfo.asp?SpID=18080 Diospyros digyna in the AgroForestryTree Database] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141223061735/http://www.worldagroforestrycentre.org/sea/Products/AFDbases/af/asp/SpeciesInfo.asp?SpID=18080 |date=2014-12-23 }}</ref> Fruiting takes about 3–4 years from seed and the trees are heavy bearers.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

==Fruit==
Black sapote [[fruit]] are [[tomato]]-like and measure {{convert|5|-|10|cm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter, with an inedible skin that turns from olive to a deep yellow-green when ripe and a pulp which is white and inedible when unripe but assumes a flavor, color and texture often likened to [[chocolate pudding]] when ripe. Fruits usually contain seeds, up to a maximum of 12.<ref name="w-a-f"/> The texture has been likened to that of a papaya. The ripe fruit may have "the taste and consistency of chocolate pudding."<ref>{{cite book|last=Boning|first=Charles R.|title=Florida's Best Fruiting Plants: Native and Exotic Trees, Shrubs, and Vines|year=2006|publisher=Pineapple Press, Inc.|location=Sarasota, Florida|page=43}}</ref>

Unripe fruits are astringent, caustic, bitter, irritating, and have been used as fish poison in the Philippines.<ref name=Morton />

==Propagation==
Propagation is usually from seed, which can retain viability for several months and require around 30 days for germination.<ref name="Morton"/> Some trees are seedless however, and can be propagated by [[air-layering]] or [[shield budding]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

==Cultivation==
Black sapote trees are normally found below 600 meters, but are not particular about soil, and can tolerate light frosts. They are sensitive to drought, requiring irrigation in dry areas, but are quite tolerant of flooding. The tree grows fairly slowly for the first 3–4 years, perhaps just 1 foot/year for the first couple of years.<ref name="Morton"/> Later however it grows much more rapidly. Trees should be spaced 10-12m apart (about 32–39 ft.).<ref name="w-a-f"/>

Growing requirements: full sunlight, grows best in most well drained soils (sand and lime-stone based) and high pH soils (5.5-7.0), mature trees can tolerate -2/-3 °C (28-30 °F) temperatures and young trees can be killed at 0 °C (32 °F) temperatures.{{cn|date=August 2024}}

Pollination takes place by insects, but some varieties are self-incompatible, meaning they require cross pollination.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HS1055/HS305: Black Sapote Growing in the Florida Home Landscape |url=https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS305 |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=edis.ifas.ufl.edu |language=en}}</ref>

==Cultivars==
The range in size of tree and hairiness of leaves; size, shape, seediness, flesh color and sweetness of fruit; and time of fruiting suggest that considerable genetic variability exists. Selections have been made and propagated in the Philippines, Australia, and Florida, USA.<ref name="encyc-fn">

===Australian cultivars===
'Bernicker' (also 'Bernecker') is a prolific producer of nearly spherical, medium to large fruit with few seeds and of superior quality.<ref name="w-a-f"/><ref name="encyc-fn" /><ref name="edis">

 | year = 2013
 | url = http://www.daleysfruit.com.au/fruit%20pages/blksapote.htm
 | access-date = 2013-03-03}}

'Mossman' has very large, round fruit of medium flavor with high pulp content and few seeds, and is capable of producing up to 450 kg per tree.<ref name="edis" /><ref name="daleys" />

'Maher' has very large, flattened fruit of good to very good quality with few seeds. It is uniquely known among cultivars for being a small, yet prolific tree (up to 4 meters).<ref name="w-a-f"/><ref name="encyc-fn" /><ref name="edis" /><ref name="daleys" />

'Ricks Late' originated in NSW Australia and produces heavy, late crops with excellent quality.<ref name="edis" /><ref name="daleys" />

'Superb' is a selection from North Queensland that bears large quantities of superb quality, small fruits that may be completely seedless if not cross pollinated.<ref name="edis" /><ref name="daleys" />

'Cocktail' is described as having excellent flavor.<ref name="edis" />

===Florida cultivars===
'Mérida' (also 'Reineke' or 'Reinecke') is named after the origin of its seed. It produces 70 kg or more of very sweet, small to medium-sized fruit of very good quality with 5-10 seeds, beginning 6–8 weeks earlier than other varieties (November in Florida).<ref name="encyc-fn" /><ref name="edis" /><ref name="type-desc">{{Citation
